newsitem.title: INDIA: U.N. chief hopes Zaire refugee airlift to proceed.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief hopes Zaire refugee airlift to proceed.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan expressed hope on Monday that plans to airlift home 100,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees from rebel-held eastern Zaire would move ahead.
On Saturday, after 48 hours of high-level pressure, the United Nations extracted an agreement from Laurent Kabila, the leader of Rwandan-backed rebels, to allow the refugees to be flown home.
But key issues need to be resolved. Rwanda has yet to confirm that it will accept planes flying the refugees straight back to the capital.
Kigali and the Rwandan-backed rebels now controlling more than a third of Zaire also have their concerns about the repatriation.

"Yesterday there were indications that the rebels have agreed to allow assistance to get to the refugees and to allow planes to go in to evacuate them," Annan told a news conference in the Indian capital.
"There have been movements and I hope it will be maintained," he said.

Annan said the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR was arranging an airlift to get as many of the refugees as possible out of Zaire. The returnees are the rump of more than two million Hutus who fled into exile in 1994.
"Some may not be in a condition to travel and they will have to be given temporary sanctuary for their situation to stabilise before they could move on," the U.N. chief said.
Annan was on the last day of a three-day visit to New Delhi to address a meeting of foreign ministers of the Non-Aligned Movement and to meet Indian officials.
